name: Velvet Crush
label: Creation Records
lede: Ric Menck and Paul Chastain left Chicago for Providence, cut their first album on Matthew Sweet's home eight-track, and got it released in Britain by Creation.

eras.title: Chicago kids on British indie labels
eras.text: Before Velvet Crush, Menck and Chastain were already a pair, cutting jangly singles under three different names. Two of those names ended up on UK labels, The Subway Organisation and Sarah Records, a long way from Chicago.

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush
years.h: Menck plays drums for the Reverbs on The Happy Forest
years.p: Ric Menck's first band of note makes a 1984 album with singer John Brabeck. Menck's instrument is the drums, though the songs are what he studies.

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush
years.h: Paul Chastain's Halo EP comes out on Pet Sounds
years.p: A solo EP, Beatles-minded and gentle. Trouser Press calls it "tender and skillfully realized."

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush · Wikipedia: Velvet Crush
years.h: Choo Choo Train signs to the UK's Subway Organisation
years.p: Menck, Chastain and guitarist Darren Cooper release the Briar Rose and High EPs on the UK label. The same two also record as Bag-O-Shells for Bus Stop and the Springfields for Sarah Records.
years.xp: Shoes' Jeff Murphy guests on Choo Choo Train's 'Every Little Knight'. The band's eleven tracks were gathered as Briar High in 1992 and again in 1998 as Hey Wimpus: The Early Recordings of Paul Chastain & Ric Menck.

eras.title: Matthew Sweet's eight-track
eras.text: In Providence the duo became a trio with guitarist Jeffrey Underhill. Their friend Matthew Sweet produced the first album at home, and Creation Records put it out in the UK the same year Menck was drumming on Sweet's own breakthrough.

years.src: Wikipedia: Velvet Crush · Trouser Press: Velvet Crush
years.h: Velvet Crush starts up in Providence, Rhode Island
years.p: Chastain sings and plays bass, Menck drums. Jeffrey Underhill, then Jeffrey Borchardt, of White Sisters and Honeybunch, plays guitar.

years.src: Wikipedia: Velvet Crush
years.h: 'If Not True' is the first Velvet Crush single
years.p: It comes out on Bus Stop, the label that had released Bag-O-Shells.

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush · Wikipedia: Velvet Crush
years.h: The Ash and Earth EP, then The Soul Crusher in Australia
years.p: Ash and Earth comes out on Bus Stop and Seminal Twang; Summershine issues The Soul Crusher e.p. in Australia.

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush · Wikipedia: Velvet Crush
yt: 'Window to the World', from the debut
years.h: Matthew Sweet records the debut at home
years.p: Sweet produces In the Presence of Greatness on his home eight-track. Creation releases it in the UK, Ringers Lactate in the US.
years.xp:
Trouser Press picked out 'Drive Me Down', 'Window to the World', 'Ash and Earth' and 'Blind Faith', and called the record "entirely true to the form but distinctly original."

Glass Records reissued it on vinyl in October 2018.

years.src: Wikipedia: Girlfriend
years.h: Menck drums on six songs on Sweet's Girlfriend
years.p: Sweet's breakthrough album splits the drum credits between Ric Menck and Fred Maher. Chastain turns up on bass and vocals on the bonus-disc reissue.

years.src: Wikipedia: Velvet Crush · Trouser Press: Velvet Crush
years.h: Creation releases 'Window to the World' and The Post-Greatness e.p.
years.p: Two more Creation records follow the album. The EP includes the band's take on 'Atmosphere'.

eras.title: Mitch Easter's North Carolina
eras.text: For the second album the band went to Mitch Easter and three North Carolina studios, with Epic's 550 Music putting it out in America. They came back with a record named after a Brian Wilson line and a tour opening for The Jesus and Mary Chain.

years.src: Wikipedia: Teenage Symphonies to God · Trouser Press: Velvet Crush
years.h: Teenage Symphonies to God, named for Brian Wilson's Smile
years.p: Mitch Easter co-produces and plays lead guitar at the Drive-In in Winston-Salem. The sleeve nods to Frank Holmes's Smile artwork.
years.xp:
The songs lean toward Gram Parsons country-rock. There's a Gene Clark cover, 'Why Not Your Baby', Stephen Duffy co-wrote 'Faster Days', and Greg Leisz plays pedal steel.

Stereo Review called it "top-to-bottom great"; Rolling Stone heard "sonic myopia." By 1999 it had sold about 20,000 copies.

years.src: Wikipedia: Teenage Symphonies to God · Omnivore Recordings: Velvet Crush
years.h: Velvet Crush opens for the Jesus and Mary Chain and Mazzy Star
years.p: The North American tour behind Teenage Symphonies to God puts the trio in front of [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]] and [[Mazzy Star|c48d4327-8122-4286-af66-05e1ee6ac4d8]] crowds.
years.xp: Omnivore's bio adds that Velvet Crush also went out as the backing band for both Matthew Sweet and Stephen Duffy.

years.cap: Velvet Crush with Tommy Keene, London
years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush
yt: Live at the Vic Theatre, Chicago, March 1995
years.h: Tommy Keene plays guitar on a Chicago show
years.p: With Tommy Keene in the touring band, a 1995 Chicago set is taped. It comes out in 2000 as Rock Concert.

years.src: Wikipedia: Velvet Crush · Trouser Press: Velvet Crush · Providence Phoenix: Velvet Crush
years.h: The band stops, and the side projects come out
years.p: Wikipedia dates Velvet Crush's first break-up to 1996. Summershine issues The Ballad of Ric Menck, home recordings from 1985–90, and Underhill's Honeybunch album Time Trails.
years.xp:
Chastain looked back on the Creation and 550 years for the Providence Phoenix in 1999: "It was a real downer time, and we were all pretty burnt out."

"We changed and our labels changed from the time we had originally signed," he said. The way back was a project "on our own terms."

eras.title: Back as a four-piece, then a duo
eras.text: The band regrouped with a second guitarist, Peter Phillips, and Easter producing again. After Underhill's last album, Velvet Crush became Menck and Chastain plus friends, with Menck working out of Los Angeles.

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush · Wikipedia: Velvet Crush · Providence Phoenix: Velvet Crush
years.h: Heavy Changes is Underhill's last album with the band
years.p: Mitch Easter produces again, Peter Phillips adds a second guitar, and the band covers Buck Owens's 'White Satin Bed'. Action Musik releases it.
years.xp: In America it got limited distribution through Parasol, and it was also released in Japan, the Providence Phoenix reported. By then Menck had moved to Los Angeles for session work and touring with [[Liz Phair|149326c2-b8a3-48e3-b3d2-9b5b9593127f]], while Chastain stayed in Rhode Island's South County.

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush · Providence Phoenix: Velvet Crush
years.h: Matthew Sweet is back for Free Expression
years.p: Menck and Chastain make the Bobsled album with Sweet, vintage synths and Greg Leisz on steel guitar. The two produce it with Sweet.

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush
years.h: Chastain's solo record turns into Soft Sounds
years.p: It started as a Chastain project and Menck's part is small. Underhill plays drums, and the record covers Scott Walker's 'Duchess'.

years.src: Trouser Press: Velvet Crush · Wikipedia: Velvet Crush
years.h: Stereo Blues, then a long pause
years.p: Adam Schmitt co-produces and Darren Cooper of Choo Choo Train plays. The band goes semi-dormant afterward.
years.xp: Menck had moved to Los Angeles and a drummer-for-hire career, working with [[Liz Phair|149326c2-b8a3-48e3-b3d2-9b5b9593127f]], Marianne Faithfull and The Tyde. Chastain stayed on the East Coast.

eras.title: Back on stage in New England
eras.text: Two decades after the Creation years, a vinyl reissue of the debut brought the original trio back together. They added The Dream Syndicate's Jason Victor on lead guitar.

years.src: Wikipedia: Velvet Crush
years.h: Peter Phillips, the band's second guitarist, dies
years.p: Phillips played with Velvet Crush from 1996 to 1999. Wikipedia lists his death in 2015 and gives no cause.

years.src: Omnivore Recordings: Pre-Teen Symphonies · Louisville Public Media: Velvet Crush's Ric Menck
years.h: Omnivore digs up the demos for Pre-Teen Symphonies
years.p: Eight demos, 'Hold Me Up' among them, plus eight songs live at the Cabaret Metro in Chicago in 1994.
years.xp: Menck talked it through with Kyle Meredith on WFPK. "We never expected to be successful in a mainstream way," he said. "We figured at best, we'd be a cult band."

years.src: Wikipedia: Velvet Crush
years.h: Glass Records reissues In the Presence of Greatness on vinyl
years.p: The Matthew Sweet-produced debut is back in print on vinyl.

years.src: Wikipedia: Velvet Crush
years.h: Underhill rejoins for a New England reunion tour
years.p: Menck, Chastain and Underhill play together again, with Jason Victor added on lead guitar.

sources.title: Louisville Public Media: Velvet Crush's Ric Menck (Kyle Meredith, 2017)
